brief.situation: You are the security manager on call at Pellham Mutual, a fictional insurer. At 02:00 ransomware began encrypting the primary data center's virtual machines using a stolen domain administrator account. Protect what you can recover from, bring the most important service back within its objectives, and write it up.
handover: BIA tiers: Claims is Tier 1 (RTO 4 hours, RPO 15 minutes); the public website is Tier 2 (RTO 24 hours); Payroll is Tier 3 (RTO 72 hours; next pay run in 5 days).

Recovery options: a warm site with continuous replication of Claims (latest point only, about 5 minutes behind); a domain-joined backup server with last night's 23:00 backups (restore about 60 minutes); an immutable cloud copy of the same 23:00 backups (restore about 180 minutes).
A failover needs a declared disaster; the executive on call declares it on your recommendation.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you close the incident you notify, record it and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Fifteen minutes until the encryption reaches the file servers is the author's figure.
Twenty minutes until replication carries encrypted data to the warm site is the author's figure (replication runs about 5 minutes behind).
Thirty minutes until the attacker deletes the domain-joined backups is the author's figure.
Twenty-five minutes until a stolen administrator account still trusted at the warm site is used again is the author's figure.
Forty minutes to fail Claims over to the warm site is the author's figure.
Sixty minutes to restore Claims from the backup server is the author's figure.
One hundred eighty minutes to restore Claims from the immutable copy is the author's figure.
Claims' RTO of 4 hours is the fictional insurer's BIA figure.
Declaring within 30 minutes is the author's teaching figure.

parts.label: Recovery points
parts.criteria: Pauses replication before it carries encrypted data, takes the domain-joined backups off the network before the attacker reaches them, and isolates the primary at the switch level.
parts.modelAnswer: I paused replication so the warm site kept the 01:55 point, disconnected BKP01 and isolated the primary at the core switches in the first 15 minutes.

parts.label: Strategy against the BIA
parts.criteria: Recovers Tier 1 first, from the only option that meets its RPO (the clean replica) within its RTO; rebuilds trust in the directory before failover so the attacker cannot follow.
parts.modelAnswer: Claims' 15-minute RPO ruled out the 23:00 backups; I verified the replica, reset privileged accounts and krbtgt, then failed over well inside the 4-hour RTO. Payroll waits; its RTO is 72 hours.

parts.label: Plan and tests
parts.criteria: Names the plan gaps (replication carries corruption; backups on the domain) and a test that would have exposed them, such as a ransomware DR simulation.
parts.modelAnswer: Continuous replication copies corruption and BKP01 sat on the domain. The next DR simulation should run a ransomware scenario against both.

expertPath.text: Map the damage to the BIA tiers. Pause replication, take BKP01 off the domain, isolate the primary at the switches.
Have the disaster declared; verify the replica (01:55, clean); reset privileged accounts and krbtgt twice.
Fail Claims over to the warm site; tell the call center and partners.
Payroll and the website follow by tier. Report through the call tree; add a ransomware scenario to the next DR simulation.

recovered.headline: Good: the strategy matched the BIA
recovered.body: Only a clean replica met Claims' RPO, so protecting it came first; rebuilding trust came before failover so the attacker could not follow.

recoveredLate.headline: Recovered, at a cost
recoveredLate.body: The criteria show what cost you: spread at the primary, a recovery past the RTO or RPO, or Tier 3 ahead of Tier 1.

reinfected.headline: The attacker followed the failover
reinfected.body: A recovery site that trusts the same stolen account is not a recovery. Reset privileged accounts and the Kerberos key first.

pointsDestroyed.headline: Recovery points destroyed
pointsDestroyed.body: Continuous replication copies corruption, and domain-joined backups are a target. Pause and disconnect them before anything else.

leftOpen.headline: The attacker can strike again
leftOpen.body: Isolate the primary and kill the stolen account before you call the night done.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No DR report was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Protect the recovery points first: pause replication before it carries encrypted data, take the domain-joined backup server off the network, and isolate the primary at the switches. The BIA puts Claims first (RTO 4 h, RPO 15 min), and only the warm-site replica at 01:55 meets that RPO; last night's backups lose about three hours. Get the disaster declared, verify the replica, rebuild trust (privileged resets, krbtgt twice, the VPN path closed) so the attacker cannot follow, then fail over. Payroll (RTO 72 h) waits. Afterwards, add a ransomware scenario to the DR simulation tests.
